Orders the leaf's mark files, stamped with CLOCK_MONOTONIC, against the gateway's Instant stage deadline. On Linux Instant reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC too; on macOS it reads CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW, so the two cannot be compared and the row is compiled on Linux only.
Binds a listener on 127.8.0.1; macOS configures only 127.0.0.1 on lo0, so other 127/8 addresses cannot be bound without an ifconfig alias (MIK-8660 T7b).

The Linux keychain reader and writer (the Secret Service through gdbus and secret-tool) are compiled on Linux only, the writer's tests in keychain_linux.rs's writer_tests with them; macOS reads and writes the keychain through security-framework, tested by keychain_macos_tests.
Writes and reads POSIX ACL xattrs (system.posix_acl_access), which only the Linux probe reads; off Linux the writer keeps owner bits only.
Not run on macOS: it checks Linux set-id semantics (a set-id mode kept across a save); the macOS behaviour is unproven, and no macOS leg runs it.
Creates a file whose name is not UTF-8; APFS refuses such a name, so the row runs on Linux, where the byte-wise name comparison it pins matters.
The full group mode survives a save only after the Linux ACL probe proves no ACL; off Linux the writer keeps owner bits only by design.
Builds a path at the Linux PATH_MAX (4096); macOS PATH_MAX is 1024, so the fixture cannot be made the same way.

APFS refuses file names that are not valid UTF-8, so no real executable can carry a non-UTF-8 argv0 on macOS; this row itself still skips macOS. macOS runs its sibling inv6_non_utf8_argv0_kept_by_capture (the same bytes through capture, with a stand-in for the file check) and inv6_non_utf8_bytes_round_trip.
Reads /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range, which exists only on Linux.
Writes to /dev/full for ENOSPC; macOS has no /dev/full.

Runs lease_t11_child in a fresh process to observe the not-dumpable mark, which only Linux and Android have; on macOS no test observes the guard's zero core limit.

Opens a child's /proc/<pid> directory and reads it after the reap, which only Linux has; the control socket judges its peer through /proc only on Linux.

Waits for a refused connect and reads a queued connect's reset, as Linux answers them; on macOS a full backlog also refuses, so a refusal there does not show the listener closed. The control socket runs only with the Linux sandbox.
Creates a directory whose name is not UTF-8, which macOS file systems refuse; the direct-URL check it pins matches the dist-info suffix on the name's bytes, the same code on every platform.
Reads /proc/net, which only Linux has; the Linux preview proxy uses it. The proxy on macOS is not wired until its own sandbox part (ADR-027).

macOS answers ESRCH for the leader's own group while a process given SIGKILL is still exiting, so there an injected ESRCH from that group is the kill of a group already gone by rule; the group a kill names comes from shared spawn and kill code, so this Linux row guards every platform.

The row creates a registry directory whose name holds the byte 0xff; APFS refuses that mkdir with errno 92 (EILSEQ), so its input cannot exist on macOS. skills list renders the path through the same display code on every platform, so the Linux run covers it.
